subject: Coordination: bundled finance systems renewal & negotiation window
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, michael.grant@redwoodinference.com, Sandra Vega <sandra.vega@pegasusbilling.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@ramp.com>
Cc: legal@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Coordination: bundled finance systems renewal & negotiation window

Team + Sandra/Tom —

Quick context: our NetSuite-billing contract is up for renewal in Q3 and Ramp (expense) also has the annual renewal window in late Q3. Given integration overlap (invoice export -> AP -> expense reimbursements) and parallel migration risk, Finance recommends we treat these two renewals as a bundled negotiation opportunity to extract transition credits and shorten duplicate maintenance.

I attached a suggested timeline (Billing_Stack_Renewal_Timeline.xlsx) — please review. Key asks for today:
- Sandra/Tom: can each vendor confirm earliest deadline for locking list price (do you have an advance-notice lock date)?
- Marcus: please validate whether a 60-day overlap with both vendors is required for GA migration of billing exports to our new ORC pipeline.
- Laura: confirm negotiation guardrails (max credit we can accept, minimum SLA/uptime we need) so we have authority to ask for credits.

Proposed approach (short):
1) Ask both vendors for 12-month renewal with an opt-out window tied to migration milestones.
2) Request a bundled credit if both renewals are executed with Redwood as sole billing orchestration — target 10–15% first-year credit + onboarding assistance.
3) Push for a 90-day price-lock notice and an integration playbook commitment (export formats, mapping, SFTP docs).

Sandra/Tom — can you each provide a high-level quote/terms by EOD 4/21? We want to surface a combined negotiation ask to Legal and Procurement next week.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Head of Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Billing_Stack_Renewal_Timeline.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Sandra Vega <sandra.vega@pegasusbilling.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, michael.grant@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:42:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Coordination: bundled finance systems renewal & negotiation window

Kimberly —

Thanks for the heads up. I attached our standard renewal quote (Pegasus_Renewal_Quote_2027-04-21.pdf). High-level:
- 12-month term available, 10% standard renewal discount for existing customers (we can talk to Sales about promotional credits for bundled purchases).
- Price-lock: we guarantee current list pricing for 60 days from the quote date (we can extend to 90 days with a signed LOI).
- Migration support: we can provide two days of onboarding assistance and a technical playbook for exports (CSV/SFTP). Additional days are billable at our professional services rate but we can include up to 5 pro-serv days with a bundled agreement.

Attachment: Pegasus_Renewal_Quote_2027-04-21.pdf (pdf)

If you want, I can jump on a 30-min call with your integration lead tomorrow to run through export formats and timelines.

Best,
Sandra Vega
Director, Strategic Accounts — Pegasus Billing
sandra.vega@pegasusbilling.com
+1 (415) 555-0147
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, michael.grant@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:07:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Coordination: bundled finance systems renewal & negotiation window

Kimberly / team —

Appreciate the summary. Quick notes after skimming Pegasus quote (cc Sandra):
- Integration: our current ORC pipeline expects a flattened invoice CSV (columns: invoice_id, customer_id, amount, tax, memo, line_items_json). Pegasus's playbook supports this but they currently put line_items as separate rows; we'll need a transform step that adds ~2 dev-weeks (risk: mapping cost).
- Overlap: we can likely operate with a 45–60 day overlap if Pegasus provides sample exports and a test SFTP earlier. 90-day lock plus LOI sounds reasonable for us if we can secure onboarding assistance.
- Credit ask: I recommend targeting 12% effective first-year credit across both vendors (10% from list + 2% onboarding credit). That should buy us the mapping work and lower first-year TCO.

I attached a short migration risk rundown (Migration_Risk_Rundown.docx) that calls out dev effort, fallback plan, and rollback window.

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — good start.

Laura's negotiation guardrails:
- Target: 12% combined first-year credit or equivalent onboarding services (professional services days) that cover integration/dev work.
- Minimum acceptable: 6% combined credit OR 5 days of included pro-serv per vendor + 30-day price lock. Anything less and we escalate to procurement for re-bid.
- SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime for billing endpoints + 30-day data-retention export on demand.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly — capture formal LOI language and ask both vendors for a 90-day price-lock LOI by 4/26.
2) Marcus — schedule a 30-min integration call with Sandra; loop Tom if Ramp will be part of a bundled ask.
3) Marissa/Michael — prep a preliminary cost comparison (NetSuite vs Pegasus) and include one-year TCO with estimated migration dev hours.

If vendors are aligned on price-lock + 10%+ onboarding support, Procurement will take an aggressive posture to get a bundled credit. If not, we run a parallel RFP to two other vendors.

-LB

Laura Bennett
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
